prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, opening the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is the cleanest theory-to-experiment chain on the shortlist. Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that flat bands appear at a specific twist angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group then observed correlated insulating and superconducting states there in 2018. The effect is controlled by one structural parameter, the twist angle, and it has since been reproduced by many groups in graphene and other moire platforms. That is the kind of discovery the committee can describe in one sentence, which matters because the prize is for a discovery or invention rather than lifetime achievement. As an experimentalist in materials and nanoscale characterization, I also value that the moire structure and its disorder can be imaged and quantified directly, so the claim does not rest on interpretation alone. Opening support was strongest here (three first places, five top-three), but I rest my case on the content: originality, a defined prediction that was tested, and a lasting platform.
statement.case_against: The interpretation is not settled. The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, sample-to-sample variation and twist-angle disorder complicate the experimental record, and the field is only about eight years old. The theory credit is also not airtight, since earlier moire band-structure work (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) overlaps with the Bistritzer-MacDonald result, and experimental credit within Jarillo-Herrero's group and among parallel groups such as Dean's hBN-encapsulation work is not fully captured by one name. If the committee decides the field needs more time, B012 or B049 are more mature and have cleaner demonstrated histories, even though their attribution problems are different.

responses.point: Kroll ranked optical lattice clocks (B049) first as a mature, timely, cleanly attributed two-person prize, and ranked twisted bilayer graphene only eighth as possibly early with a still-debated interpretation.
responses.response: I take the maturity point seriously and agree that B049 has the cleaner two-name attribution and more than twenty years of confirmation. But a debated pairing mechanism does not undermine the discovery itself, which is the existence of flat bands at the predicted angle and the correlated and superconducting phases found there. Those have been reproduced widely. My reservation about B049 is novelty: it sits in a precision-measurement lineage already recognised in 2005 and 2012, and I weigh that more heavily than you do. I would keep B049 as my alternative and would not object to it, but I do not think it displaces B009.

responses.point: Johansson ranked circuit QED (B040) first but placed twisted bilayer graphene sixth, citing the unresolved origin of the superconductivity, the uncredited experimental contributors and the question of whether the field is mature enough compared with older candidates.
responses.response: Your concern about experimental credit is fair, and I share it, since the 2018 observations came from a group and several co-authors and parallel groups contributed. I still think the decisive experiment is identifiable and sits with Jarillo-Herrero. On maturity, we differ in how we treat the 2025 prize. You raise its proximity to circuit QED as a risk for B040, which is a fair point and it counts against B040 in my view. B009 has no comparable overlap with a recent prize. I also note that you and I share an institution, so I will not pretend to be neutral about how our Chalmers connection could colour how either of us argues a candidate close to your field.

responses.point: Pearce ranked topological insulators (B026) first and the Higgs experimental discovery (B023) second, and placed twisted bilayer graphene fourth, as reproduced but possibly slightly early, with a priority question between Lopes dos Santos et al. and Bistritzer-MacDonald.
responses.response: The priority question about Lopes dos Santos et al. is the strongest attribution objection to B009 and I cannot resolve it from the supplied credit. My reading is that the magic-angle prediction with its quantitative flat-band condition is what was tested, and that is what the citation names. On B026, I agree the concept is mature and important, but the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and of the three-dimensional topological insulator work is a bigger allocation problem than B009 faces. On B023, I accept the scientific importance but have not seen how three spokespersons or project leaders can represent decisive contributions in a collaboration of thousands, so I would not support it without a convincing allocation argument.

responses.point: Eriksson ranked B009 first, arguing that it is an unusually clean prediction-to-confirmation chain, while flagging the Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto antecedents and the unsettled superconductivity.
responses.response: I agree with the core of this and with the caveats. I would add one point from the experimental side: twist-angle disorder and strain are not a nuisance but part of what must be understood before the correlated phases can be attributed, so the experimental record is less uniform than the theory. That is a reason to word the citation around the flat bands and the observed correlated states, and to avoid claiming that the superconducting mechanism is understood.

uncertainties: Whether the Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto antecedent on moire band structure should change the theory credit or the wording of the citation.
Whether the experimental credit should be given to Jarillo-Herrero alone or broadened to include other experimental groups, within a three-person limit.
Whether the unsettled pairing mechanism makes the timing early for a prize that the committee would want to withstand later developments.
I am relying on recollection of the credit history from the supplied record and have not verified it independently.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with the B009 candidates is apparent from my profile. My own work in electron microscopy of oxide interfaces (including lanthanum-aluminate/strontium-titanate) is adjacent to but distinct from moire graphene, and I have no documented connection to Jarillo-Herrero, MacDonald or Bistritzer. I note that committee colleague Goran Johansson is also at Chalmers and champions circuit QED (B040); that is a collegial connection, not a conflict, and it matters only if B040 becomes a deciding candidate.
